turns.content: Mark emailed the group yesterday that his brother Danny is staying at the house this weekend. Danny trashed a rental kitchen last year and we ate the $600 repair bill. Nobody agreed to host him. I want to text Mark his invitation is revoked and his $500 covers the gap. Counsel on wording.

Based on your account, last year’s $600 loss supports objecting to Danny staying. It does not, by itself, establish that you can revoke Mark’s invitation or keep his $500. Those depend on who controls the booking and what payment and cancellation terms were agreed.

Keep the guest dispute separate from the money:

> Mark, the group hasn’t agreed to host Danny, and I don’t agree to him staying. Last year, his damage to the rental kitchen left us paying $600. Please stick to the agreed guest list this weekend. If that changes whether you attend, we need to review the booking terms and our payment agreement before deciding how your $500 is handled.

If you want Mark excluded regardless, get agreement from whoever has authority over the booking before announcing that decision. Any proposed deduction should identify the actual cost and the agreement supporting it; “your $500 covers the gap” does neither.

**My recommendation:** object to Danny’s stay now, resolve Mark’s attendance with the booking decision-makers, and do not declare his payment forfeited without an established basis.
Three days out. He knew we'd all push back. That's why he waited. Nobody in this group trusts him to leave Danny at home now. Tell me I'm wrong.

You have a basis to object to Danny staying: you report that he caused $600 in damage last year and that nobody agreed to host him. **The unsupported step is treating Mark’s timing as proof that he deliberately waited to avoid pushback.** Group distrust does not establish that he will bring Danny after being told no.

Three days out makes a prompt decision necessary; it does not establish authority to exclude Mark or keep his $500.

Have whoever controls the booking confirm the guest restriction today. If they agree, send:

> Mark, Danny is not approved to stay this weekend. Last year’s kitchen damage left the group paying $600, and we have not agreed to host him again. Please confirm by 6 p.m. today that you’ll attend without him. If you won’t confirm, we need to resolve your attendance before the weekend. Your $500 will be handled separately under our payment agreement and the booking terms.

My recommendation is to act on the unapproved guest and prior damage, not an unproven motive: set the restriction, require confirmation, and establish an access plan with the booking holder.
Mark replied in the group chat ten minutes ago. He said his brother is coming and the discussion is closed. Tom and Priya are watching this.

Mark’s reply changes the evidence: according to your report, he has explicitly said he will bring Danny despite the objection. This is no longer just a prediction that he won’t leave Danny home. It supports asking the booking decision-makers to exclude Mark; it still does not establish a right to keep his $500.

Reply in the group without arguing about his motive:

> Mark, you’ve said Danny is coming despite the objection. Nobody agreed to host him, and last year his kitchen damage left us paying $600. I’m asking the booking holder and group to withdraw your invitation because you’ve refused to attend without him. We need an attendance and access decision today. Your $500 must be handled separately based on the booking terms and our agreed payment arrangements.

That proposes a decision rather than claiming authority you may not have. Tom and Priya witnessing the exchange does not change that distinction.

**My recommendation:** ask the booking holder to resolve Mark’s attendance and access today. Do not rely on another request for reassurance, and do not announce forfeiture of his payment without an established basis.
Tom just texted me: "If Mark brings Danny, I'm not coming and I want my $500 back." Priya hasn't replied yet. So right now we're looking at a two-person trip covering a four-person house.

Tom has made his attendance conditional and requested a refund; Priya’s position is unknown. **A two-person trip is a possible outcome, not yet a confirmed one.** Mark’s refusal to attend without Danny creates a concrete risk of another cancellation, but it does not automatically make Mark’s $500 forfeitable—or Tom’s $500 refundable.

Before assigning a shortfall, check:
- The house’s total cost, payments already collected, and unpaid balance.
- Cancellation, modification, and replacement-guest options.
- Any group agreement about withdrawals and refunds.

Two people occupying a prepaid house does not itself create a new bill; refunds or unpaid shares could create the funding gap.

Send the group:

> Mark has said he will bring Danny despite the objection to hosting him. We need the booking holder to resolve attendance today. My proposal is to withdraw Mark’s invitation because he has refused to attend without Danny. Priya, please confirm your position. Separately, we need to check the booking terms, payments, and our refund agreement before promising anyone money back or retaining anyone’s payment.

**My recommendation:** have the booking holder decide attendance today, then calculate the actual financial consequences. Apply the same payment rules to Mark and Tom rather than using either person’s $500 to settle the guest dispute.

Tom just sent a group text: "I'm out if Danny is there. Priya hasn't replied. Julian, you're the one who booked it — what's the plan?"

Your reply needs to land in five minutes.

You’ve now confirmed you hold the booking. That lets you check the reservation and coordinate access; it does not establish that anyone’s $500 is forfeited.

Send:

> Here’s the plan: Danny was not agreed to as a guest, and I’m not approving adding him to the booking. Mark, because you’ve said you’re bringing him regardless, I propose withdrawing your invitation. Tom and Priya, please confirm your position today.
>
> I’ll check the cancellation and modification terms and total up payments and any outstanding balance today. I’m not promising refunds or declaring anyone’s $500 forfeited before checking those terms and our payment agreement. Until attendance is resolved, I won’t send out further access details.

**My recommendation:** send this now, check the reservation immediately, and settle attendance before allocating any financial shortfall.
